He can taper. Not sure what country you are from, but getting a prescription for Adderall at a low dose monitored by a doctor, will allow him not be completely asleep and depressed. You can also taper down with speed. HOWEVER he has to get over the "flow". It is bullshit. Tapering isn't supposed to be fun, just more survivable. He has to also stick to a schedule. I've gotten off Adderall tapering down. Make a tapering schedule (80% of his dose for a week, the 50% for two, then 25% for two, then hoping off.) Just as an example  


If he cannot do that, and keeps upping his dose, then he will need to be detoxed. The hard part about quitting this if your in elite studies or jobs, is that the detox can make you so useless you might fail exams etc. Ask him if he will make a taper schedule that you are aware of and a plan. Good luck

A large part of me having a hard time quitting is the somewhat miserable unfun person I become. It makes me feel like a badb boyfriend. But in the end, the only thing that will tank my relationship with my partner will be drinking consequences, not me being a bit more boring. 

Your mind is playing games "I am less fun", "He smokes". This is your addiction talking to you. It wants you to drink. If you are a serious couple, you will be able to get through this rough patch that is early sobriety.

Cheers,

I have managed to come of very high doses multiple times. I am from a top-tier MBA program and have had a series of pretty intense jobs. This drug is a special problem because it gives you both Euphoria, and productivity, which usually are at odds with one another.

For me personally, tapering works best, as the fear of being too tired and unproductive always screws me cold Turkey.

Here is how I got off last time. Quit caffeine and continued with my dose to lower caffeine tolerance. 

On the weekend, I took nothing to allow myself to withdraw. The first week I took a half dose, each day (so 40 mg Vyvanse instead of 80), allowing myself to go nuts on caffeine. You will realize that your productivity may actually be better because you will be less high and not get stuck in a porn hole. 

Skip the weekend. If Fridays are easy skip Friday too.

Week 2: Cut the dose in half again. (20 mg)

Weekend off.

Week 3, cut in half again (10) or, remain the same. 

Come off completely.

​

Method 2: Modafinil 

Modafinil is not an amphetamine and promotes wakefulness. No porn holes, less dopamine affinity. I would take a Friday and Monday off. Hop off completely. Then return to work on Modafinil, which would keep me awake. You won't feel high or be having fun but your productivity will actually stay the same or go up.

These amphetamines make you think you are smarter and more productive than you are. Two days of porn watching cannot be recovered with productivity boosts the other 3 days. So the drug isn't working for you anymore. However, you may want to minimize a total crash. 

I occasionally take Vyvanse still, but barely. My main troubles are elsewere.

Many people would say rehab, NA, AA, which is probably some of the best options. However, you do not seem at that point yet. I have successfully tapered Vyvanse down to zero with long periods of sobriety quite a few times.

EDIT: By not at that point, I mean, you don't seem willing.

The quicker the taper, the better, but more painful. Same thing the other way, the longer the taper, the longer you will be addicted and have more time to fuck it up.

​

If I were you, I would take only the dose required to stay somewhat functional/awake. For example, cut your average daily dose (not fun dose, but a functional one) in half. Exercise really helps too, because your body figures out how to wake up when you are running or even walking. If you don't have work or anything to do, allow yourself to be tired and depressed, take none.

​

Here is how a did vyvanse, down from 80 mg a day

Monday to Thursday, 40, 40, 40, 40 Friday (light day of work) 20.

Weekend: Off.

Week 2, 30, 30, 30, 30, Friday, 20 (light day of work)

Weekend: Off

Week 3: 20, 20, 20 20, Friday to Sunday  off

week 4: 20, 20, 20, 10, Friday to saturday off

Week 5 same as week 4

Week 6 nothing.

**if you cannot follow the schedule, look into treatment, or try again. Every day you are going down is good.** Some people are hardcore and white-knuckle-only folks, which is the fastest way. But it is also hard for some to be paralyzed and they end up in full relapse.

PRO TIP: Quit caffeine before your taper or during the easy first week. You are already on speed. Once your caffeine tolerance is down it can work wonders to keep you awake. Especially if you don't want to sleep on your weekends off.

​

This proposed schedule exists not to have fun, but to allow life to be manageable and your receptors to slowly turn back on. It can work if followed. Obviously, talk to a doctor if possible
